title: Amendment No. 1, Microsoft Volume Licensing Enrollment for Education Solutions Agreement - Softchoice, Inc. - Technology Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Microsoft Volume Licensing Enrollment for Education Solutions Agreement by and between District and Softchoice, Inc., Toronto, ON, for the latter to provide districtwide Microsoft licensed software, as specified in Softchoice, Inc., Quote No. Q-1162072, dated August 4, 2022, at an annual cost not to exceed $186,243.15, for a total new three-year cumulative cost not to exceed $558,729.45, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $466,138.35 to $1,024,867.80 and extending the term of the Agreement from October 24, 2019 through October 23, 2022 to October 23, 2025. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $558,729.45 to keep Microsoft software licenses from Softchoice through October 2025
summary: This amendment extends the district's Microsoft software licensing agreement with Softchoice, Inc. for three more years, from October 2022 to October 2025, at up to $186,243.15 per year. The most the district can spend under the agreement rises from $466,138.35 to $1,024,867.80. The software is used districtwide.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment, Community-Based Organization (CBO) Master Contract Exhibit Coversheet - Alameda County Health Care Services Agency - Nutrition Education and Obesity Prevention Program - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of an Amendment, Community-Based Organization Master Contract Coversheet and Exhibits A-F, Master Contract 900322 (aka Procurement Contract 24249), by and between the District and Alameda County Health Care Services Agency, San Leandro, CA, for the latter to provide $280,000.00 in funding to support Nutrition Education and Obesity Prevention Programs, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023.  All other terms and condition of the Master Contract remain in full force and effect.
headline: Accepts $280,000 from Alameda County for nutrition education and obesity prevention programs
summary: The Alameda County Health Care Services Agency will give the district $280,000 to support nutrition education and obesity prevention programs run by the Community Schools and Student Services Department. This amends an existing master contract with community-based organizations (Master Contract 900322). The funding covers October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023.
vendor_name: Alameda County Health Care Services Agency
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: First 5 (Five) of Alameda County - Contract for Services - Kindergarten Readiness - Neighborhoods Ready for School - Summer Learning Programs - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of First Five of Alameda County Contract for Services (Contract Number PS-NRS-2223-142) by and between the District and First Five of Alameda County, Alameda, CA, with District accepting Grant Award from the latter, in the amount of $227,000.00, for Kindergarten Readiness supporting Summer Pre-K (SPK) programs and Early Childhood Education (ECE) and K-12 teachers with professional development and orientation to the SPK model; and Kindergarten Readiness Director to develop and implement year-round school readiness and transition programming including a student passport/snapshot form, and a variety of family/child learning activities, via the Early Childhood Education Department, for the period of July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2023.
headline: Accepts $227,000 from First Five of Alameda County for kindergarten readiness and Summer Pre-K
summary: First Five of Alameda County is giving the district a $227,000 grant to support Summer Pre-K programs and to train early childhood and K-12 teachers on the Summer Pre-K model. The money also pays for a Kindergarten Readiness Director to build year-round school readiness and transition programming for families and children. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Bay Area Community Resources - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Bay Area Community Resources, San Rafael, CA, for the latter to place Climate Corps AmeriCorps Fellows in District, to support greenhouse gas reduction programs or other sustainability projects, such as implementing programs that save energy, water, or waste; educating students in classrooms or online; developing Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Climate Action Plans, and other capacity-building documents; outreach to raise community engagement; ideally average minimum of 24 hours per week to directly working on emissions, water, waste, or energy reduction projects, more specifically delineated in Exhibit A (Scope of Work), via Community Schools and Student Services Department,  for the period of September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $112,000.00.
headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $112,000 for Climate Corps fellows on sustainability projects
summary: The district will pay Bay Area Community Resources up to $112,000 to place Climate Corps AmeriCorps Fellows in the district. Fellows work on projects to cut greenhouse gas emissions, energy, water and waste, and they also teach students and help with community outreach. The agreement runs September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Saving Shorty - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Saving Shorty, Modesto, CA, for the latter to provide staff to be present on campuses determined by District to provide a positive presence during passing periods and breaks to further feelings of safety among students and staff and support a violence and disruptive-free transition between passing periods, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period August 8, 2022 through December 31, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $90,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $90,000 for Saving Shorty staff to provide a positive presence on campuses
summary: Saving Shorty will provide staff on campuses the district chooses to be present during passing periods and breaks. The goal is to help students and staff feel safe and to support calm transitions between classes. The agreement began August 8, 2022, before this board approval, and runs through December 31, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Trina Fields - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Trina Fields, Rohnert Park, CA, for the latter to work directly with Expanded Learning Office to implement an Arts Enrichment initiative that will support all 51 of District’s elementary schools ranging from theater, culinary, and music; organize and schedule a variety of Saturday (9-hour) camps, across District serving over 100+ students during each event; project manage the Salesforce Trailhead Professional Development (PD) platform for the Expanded Learning Office, all as delineated in Exhibit A of the Agreement, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $93,600.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $93,600 for a contractor to run arts enrichment and Saturday camps for elementary students
summary: The district is approving a contract with an individual consultant who works with the Expanded Learning Office on an arts enrichment initiative (theater, culinary and music) for all 51 elementary schools. The consultant also schedules Saturday camps serving 100 or more students per event and manages a professional development platform for the office. Work began September 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Hatchuel Tabernik & Associates, Inc - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Hatchuel Tabernik & Associates, Inc., Berkeley, CA, for the latter to provide planning assistance for 21st CCLC and ASSETS grant applications, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of September 2, 2022 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $67,980.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $67,980 for Hatchuel Tabernik & Associates to plan after-school grant applications
summary: Hatchuel Tabernik & Associates will help the district plan its applications for 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) and ASSETS grants, which fund after-school programs. The agreement began September 2, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - HERO - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and HERO, Oakland, CA, for the latter to implement organized recess games and physical activity sessions and provide additional support at recess while leading safe organized games, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, at East Oakland Pride Elementary School, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of September 8, 2022 through November 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $19,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $19,000 for HERO to lead organized recess games at East Oakland Pride Elementary
summary: HERO will run organized recess games and physical activity sessions and give extra support at recess at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The agreement began September 8, 2022, before this approval, and runs through November 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 4, Professional Services Contract 2019-2020 - Springboard Collaborative - Elementary Literacy Intervention Services - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 4, Professional Services Contract 2019-2020 by and between the District and Springboard Collaborative, Philadelphia, PA, for the latter to provide an eight-week after school small group elementary literacy intervention program for fifty students, each location, at  Reach Academy, Grass Valley Elementary, and Garfield Elementary Schools, including family engagement and incentives, and Professional Management, Professional Development, all as described in Exhibit A of Agreement, in an additional amount of $160,500.00, increasing the Contract not-to-exceed amount from $1,564,540.00 to $1,725,040.00, for the period May 15, 2020 through February 20, 2023,  via the Community Schools and Student Services Department. All other terms and conditions of the Contract remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $160,500 to Springboard Collaborative's after-school literacy program at three elementary schools
summary: This is the fourth amendment to the district's contract with Springboard Collaborative for an eight-week after-school small-group reading program for fifty students at each of three schools. It includes family engagement, incentives and staff training. It adds $160,500, raising the contract limit from $1,564,540 to $1,725,040, and runs through February 20, 2023.
schools: Reach Academy; Grass Valley Elementary; Garfield Elementary
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Be the Change Consulting - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Be the Change Consulting, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide monthly facilitation of the George Floyd Resolution Team, including development of agenda, tools, and supplemental materials, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of August 1, 2022 through December 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $37,500.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $37,500 for Be the Change Consulting to facilitate the George Floyd Resolution Team
summary: Be the Change Consulting will facilitate monthly meetings of the George Floyd Resolution Team, including preparing agendas, tools and supporting materials. The agreement began August 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through December 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Myrna Wright - Talent / Human Resources Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Myrna Wright, Petaluma, CA, for the latter to provide 1000 hours of consulting services to the Talent Division for the project management of the Frontline Implementation Project to coordinating planning sessions between teams, departments, and Frontline; develop communications materials and conduct outreach relevant stakeholder groups; document processes and develop training materials and sessions; and provide ongoing communication and support to employees and supervisors after the initial rollout of the Frontline solutions, via Talent / Human Resources Department, for the period of July 5, 2022 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $89,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $89,000 for a consultant to manage the rollout of Frontline HR software
summary: The district is approving a contract with an individual consultant for up to 1,000 hours of project management on the Frontline Implementation Project for the Talent Division. The work includes coordinating planning sessions, writing communications and training materials, and supporting employees and supervisors after rollout. Work began July 5, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Nadja Conway - Talent / Human Resources Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Nadja Conway, San Jose, CA, for the latter to facilitate edTPA and CalTPA Overview Sessions for small groups of teachers, provide individualized coaching as they prepare to submit the edTPA or CalTPA, monitor teacher progress, and meet monthly with the New Teacher Support & Development team to reflect on progress and discuss next steps to ensure teacher success, via Talent / Human Resources Department, for the period of July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $22,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $22,000 for a contractor to coach teachers through teaching credential assessments
summary: The district is approving a contract with an individual coach who will lead overview sessions and give individual coaching to small groups of teachers preparing for the edTPA and CalTPA teacher performance assessments. The coach also tracks progress and meets monthly with the New Teacher Support & Development team. Work began July 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - GIBCO Environmental Service - Risk Management Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and GIBCO Environmental Service, Richmond, CA, for the latter to provide environmental related services to reduce risk at the school sites, including but are not limited to environmental clean-up and collecting environmental samples, via Risk Management Department, for the period of July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for GIBCO Environmental Service to clean up and sample school sites
summary: GIBCO Environmental Service will provide environmental services to reduce risk at school sites, including environmental clean-up and collecting environmental samples. The agreement began July 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Sole Source Exemption to Public Bidding and Resolution No. 2223-0007 - Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) - Special Education Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2223-0007 - Authorizing Use of Sole Source Exception to Public Bidding for Contract by and between the District and Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI), Milwaukee, WI, and approving Services Agreement 2022-2023 between the Parties, for the latter Party to provide - 500 Verbal Intervention licenses; - Five on-site, Nonviolent Crisis Response training sessions that each accommodate up to 40 people, led by CPI Instructors; and - Eight slots for OUSD staff to become trained as trainers in Nonviolent Crisis Response for the purpose of training newly-hired personnel, via the Special Education Department, for the period of October 6, 2022 through December 31, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $234,000.00
headline: Pays Crisis Prevention Institute up to $234,000 for nonviolent crisis response training, without bidding
summary: The district is hiring the Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) for 500 verbal intervention licenses, five on-site Nonviolent Crisis Response training sessions of up to 40 people each, and training for eight district staff to become trainers. The district is skipping public bidding under a sole-source exception, which is approved by Resolution No. 2223-0007. The agreement runs October 6, 2022 through December 31, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Student Travel - Grantmakers for Education Conference - Austin Texas - Oakland High School
official_text: Approval of Board Resolution No. 2223-0009 - Authorization for Approval of Student Travel - by Oakland High School, for 2 Students (Grade 12) and 2 Adults, as specified in Out of State Field Trip/Excursion Request, attached, to attend Grantmakers for Education Conference, Austin, Texas, as described in itinerary, for the period October 18, 2022 through October 20, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves out-of-state trip to Austin, Texas for two Oakland High students and two adults at no cost
summary: Under Resolution No. 2223-0009, two Oakland High School 12th-grade students and two adults may travel to the Grantmakers for Education Conference in Austin, Texas. The trip is October 18 through October 20, 2022, at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Former Parker School Facilities - CEQA Exemption - Chief Governance Officer
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2223-0031 - Finding the Proposal to Use Former Parker School Facilities for Oakland Adult and Career Education Exempt from CEQA Evaluation and Directing the Superintendent or Her Designee to Prepare and File a Notice of Exemption
headline: Finds use of the former Parker School site for adult and career education exempt from CEQA review
summary: Resolution No. 2223-0031 finds that using the former Parker School facilities for Oakland Adult and Career Education is exempt from review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). It also directs the Superintendent or her designee to prepare and file a Notice of Exemption.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Appointment - Jeffrey Hall - Audit Committee - President, Board of Education
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of President of Board’s appointment of Jeffrey Hall (1st Term) to the Audit Committee, effective October 7, 2022, for unexpired term ending January 31, 2024.
headline: Ratifies the Board President's appointment of a member to the Audit Committee through January 2024
summary: The Board is ratifying the Board President's appointment of Jeffrey Hall, in his first term, to the Audit Committee. The appointment takes effect October 7, 2022 and fills an unexpired term ending January 31, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
